items.title: Rosenthal potential and pure equilibrium
items.statement: Every finite unweighted congestion game in the Rosenthal model has an exact potential and at least one pure Nash equilibrium.
assumptions: Each strategy is a subset of resources
Resource delay is a function of the number of users
items.scope_note: Does not apply to all weighted congestion games; does not bound Price of Anarchy.

items.title: Pure equilibria may fail in weighted congestion
items.statement: There are weighted congestion games, including weighted network games, that do not admit a pure Nash equilibrium.
items.scope_note: Existence can be recovered under special assumptions, including some linear delay settings; this is a counterexample to universal existence.

items.title: PoA for finite unweighted linear-latency congestion games
items.statement: For finite congestion games with nonnegative linear latency functions and social cost defined as the sum of players' costs, the tight pure price of anarchy bound is 5/2.
assumptions: Sum of player costs as objective
items.scope_note: Not a claim for arbitrary latency functions, weighted games, or all definitions of social cost.

items.title: Illustrative Bayesian equilibrium in first-price auction
items.statement: For n risk-neutral bidders with i.i.d. values uniform on [0,1] in a standard single-item first-price auction, bidding (n−1)/n times private value is a symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium.
items.scope_note: An illustrative equilibrium formula, not a universal PoA guarantee.

items.title: Truthful bidding is weakly dominant in standard second-price auction
items.statement: In a standard single-item second-price auction with private values and quasilinear payoff, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy.
items.scope_note: Does not claim truthful equilibria are the only Nash equilibria.

items.title: EFX is distinct from EFX0
items.statement: In the standard indivisible-goods setting, EFX checks removal of any positively valued item, while a stronger EFX0 variant also checks items of zero value.
items.scope_note: Definitions may differ when chores, mixed items, or externalities are allowed.
